title: Game profile
description: One game's profile in the game database (data/games/<id>.json). The id is the file name. Optional fields are omitted when empty or at their default. See README.md, 'Contributing to the game database'.

name.description: Display name, as the stores list the game.

description.description: One sentence on what the game is, shown only in the database browser: modes, perspective, genres and series in PCGamingWiki's pattern ("X is a singleplayer first-person shooter game in the Y series."), in our own words. Starts with the game's name. Doesn't repeat what other fields (e.g. store_details) say, such as what a bundle includes.

released.description: The game's first Windows release, earliest region: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM / YYYY when only that much is verified. A bundle, Gold, Complete, GOTY or Classic edition takes its base game's date; an Enhanced Edition, Remaster or Anniversary Edition its own.

exe.description: The main game executable's file name only (no folders), with its exact case, e.g. "DeusEx.exe". Used to pick the right folder when scanning an install.

stores.description: Where the game is sold. Omit a store entirely when the game isn't sold there.

eax.description: How the game does 3D audio, which EAX versions it supports, and whether EAX works on the current build.

versions.description: Supported EAX versions, from a verifiable source.

status.description: supported; removed_by_patch (an update stripped EAX from the current build); not_implemented (a remaster/rewrite that never had EAX); built_in (EAX already works in this build without the script, e.g. it ships its own OpenAL32.dll with EAX).

problem.description: Why the current build is in the state `status` describes.

fix.description: How to get a build where EAX works.

fix_in_place.description: true when `fix` works on the same install the script is pointed at (e.g. a Steam beta branch), so the script warns and offers to continue instead of blocking.

install.description: What the install itself does differently for this game.

tweaks.description: Advanced Compatibility Tweaks recommended for this game (default-yes prompts).

alsoft_ini.description: Settings offered on top of the generated alsoft.ini (section -> key -> value). Only these keys are allowed.

game_config.description: Changes to the game's own config files, offered in the Game Settings step.

audio_settings.description: Settings that turn on EAX and 3D sound (or make them sound right), so the player doesn't have to.

optional_settings.description: Optional quality-of-life settings and fixes that aren't needed for EAX (e.g. Quake 4's low-res textures).

sources.description: Pages backing this entry's claims, listed as links at the end of the game profile screen. Each is a URL, or {title, url} to show a name instead of the site's address.

notes.description: Caveats not covered by the other fields.

id.description: Steam AppID / GOG game ID, verified against the store. For GOG, use the game's own ID as Heroic installs it (its appName, the same as the gameId in the game's goggame-<id>.info) — for a game sold inside a pack or collection, the game inside it, never the pack.

delisted.description: Pulled from sale; existing owners keep access.

api.description: Overrides eax.api for this store's build only.

beta_branch.description: Steam only: the BetaKey of a branch that restores EAX.

extra_exe_folders.description: GOG only: other folders under the game's exe folder that hold their own exe (e.g. expansions launched from the same title) and get the same game-folder files.

companion_apps.description: Steam only: AppIDs of other Steam apps that run this game's exe from its own folder (e.g. DOOM 3's Resurrection of Evil, 9070, which starts Doom3.exe with its own arguments). Each has its own Proton prefix and launch options, so an install sets those up the same way as the game's own.

store_details.description: What's specific to this store's listing. A game that isn't an Enhanced Edition, remaster or remake doesn't mention one, unless the store sells them as one bundle (then name every game in it).

name_part.description: A config section or key name.

value.description: A string sets the value; true/false turns a dark_cfg flag on or off; null deletes the key.

format.description: ini: [Section] key=value. flat_ini: key=value lines with no [sections]. idtech_cfg: seta key "value". dark_cfg: NewDark key value, bare flags, ;flag = off. brace_cfg: {key} = {value} lines (Fallout Tactics' bos.cfg). gadb: Monolith's binary game database (F.E.A.R.'s Profile000.gdb); only switches an existing on/off setting, values "0"/"1".

locations.description: Where to look, in order, as "base:path". The first one that exists is used.

if_missing.description: When no location exists. Omitted: ask the player to launch the game once, then check again. skip: leave out this file's part of each setting and tell the player. create: create it.

crash_marker.description: A file in the same folder that the game creates while running and deletes when quit normally. If it's left behind, the game resets this config file on its next start, so it's removed (when the game isn't running) before this file is changed. Never restored on uninstall.

title.description: Enable / Fix / Remove / Raise + the result, e.g. "Enable EAX reverb".

reason.description: What the game does out of the box, in one or two short sentences.

only_if.description: Conditions for offering the setting; it's skipped silently otherwise.

speakers.description: The Speaker Configuration answer: stereo, headphones (Stereo, then Headphones), matrix, surround (any surround layout), or one exact layout (quad, surround51, surround61, surround71). A list matches any of its values.

changes.description: file -> section -> key -> value for ini files; file -> key -> value for cfg files. Files must be defined in game_config.files.

follow_up.description: Something the player does after installing, shown in the final summary.
